grades_note: S: supported by a prospective or fresh registered test; S-dt: S (design-time); S-dt-dir-size: S (design-time), direction only, on a claim about a size; D-measured: a registered synthetic reading says the test can decide; D-unknown: decidability unknown; D-weak: weak by design. A D decidable only after 2030-01-15 is D-pending at the same grades (ruling R8.4b). N, L and W are graded by their code and need no qualifier.
end_goal_note: end-goal convention (ruling R8.12b, bookkeeping only, never shown alone): a row the mapping marks withdrawn_with_reason (withdrawn under every outcome, with the reason stated in the ledger), registered_undecidable or no_target counts as honestly narrowed, graded end_goal_grade; 'requires' names the registration that must be cited at the ledger state for the mark to apply
composite_note: official rule (user ruling 2026-11-07, fourteenth set, R8.16a): a W in a composite status grades the row W; otherwise the row is graded by its first code, the status of what the row shows now (the trailing D is the pending decider, a trailing L the internals label). The earlier default (mapping default-v1) took the highest code.
split_note: split rule (user rulings 2026-11-07: R8.16b, fourteenth set, results/dataprep/rulings/user_rulings_2026-11-07.json sha256 c0886864; R8.17a and R8.17d, fifteenth set, results/dataprep/rulings/user_rulings_2026-11-07b.json sha256 7602157b). A row carrying split_of {parent: P, parent_status: S0, piece_status_at_split: s_i} is a piece of the ledger row P, whose status was S0 when it was split, and the piece's own status at the split was s_i; P's entry lists its pieces in split_into. Weight (R8.16b, R8.17d): the parent's display weight W_P is the largest display weight among the pieces present at the ledger state, and piece i weighs w_i = W_P * d_i / sum_j d_j, d being each piece's own display weight (C01's three pieces 2/3 each; C30-scen 4/3 and C30-fc 2/3). Grade (R8.17a, removing only the uplift the split itself created): g_P is P's grade at S0 under the composite-first rule, from P's own mapping entry; m0 is the pieces' weighted mean grade (weights w_i) at their at-split statuses s_i and m1 at their current statuses; the split uplift is u = max(0, m0 - g_P); if u > 0 every piece's grade is multiplied by max(0, m1 - u) / m1, so the pieces' weighted mean becomes m1 - u. The at-split statuses must have unconditional qualifiers, so m0 is fixed by the mapping. Guarantee: the pieces together weigh exactly W_P; at the statuses of the split their mean grade is at most g_P (a split cannot raise its part's weight or grade); a later status change of a piece moves the part by exactly that change's weighted grade (later evidence counts in full). This implements R8.17a's stated intent; the literal reading 'never above g_P' would also freeze later evidence. Uniform scaling can show a piece below its own grade (display only: the part score depends only on the pieces' weighted sum, the same as capping only the piece above the parent). Before a split only P is present and is graded and weighted as P.
